title: Hosted SSE: Partial-response recovery and client resume/backoff compatibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported reproducible cases where Hosted API SSE streams terminate mid-response and client SDKs display partial outputs. In several incidents the upstream generator continued producing tokens server-side while the client experienced a network disconnect or intermediate proxy reset, leading to: 1) visible truncated responses in user UIs, 2) duplicated tokens when clients attempted naive resume, and 3) state divergence when KV cache / request-level metadata were not persisted across reconnects. The scope of this ticket covers the Hosted control plane and runtime server behavior for SSE streams (not Dedicated/Private deployment config), plus compatibility adjustments in our reference JS and Python SDKs to ensure safe resume/backoff patterns for customers. Goals: make server behavior idempotent for resume attempts, ensure single-delivery semantics for completed chunks, and provide a safe fallback for clients that cannot resume (graceful polling).
acceptance_criteria: SSE streams include a monotonically increasing 'stream_pos' and finalization marker so clients can detect complete responses
Server implements an explicit resume window (30s) with robust idempotency checks to avoid double-emission
Reference JS and Python SDKs include new resume/backoff helpers and tests demonstrating no duplication with simulated mid-stream disconnects
No production regressions in latency P50/P95 for streaming endpoints (within 10% of baseline)
Instrumentation added: metric 'sse.partial_deliveries' and alert when rate > 0.1% of streaming requests
Customer-facing postmortem + mitigation steps published for affected customers
comments: 2026-03-01 09:12 - Aisha Patel: Initial customer reports from FinanceCorp and AtlasDocs. Both observed truncated outputs in web clients; AtlasDocs triggered a support escalation. Collected request IDs and sample SSE logs (attached).

2026-03-02 14:45 - Liam O'Connor: Reproduced locally by injecting a TCP RST at 80% completion on stream. Observed server continued generation and freed the generator VM, so reconnect saw a new request ID and re-generated tokens -> duplication on client if naive resume attempted.

2026-03-03 11:00 - Sergey Ivanov (runtime): Root cause hypothesis: absence of durable last-event checkpoint for SSE flows and non-idempotent generator lifecycle on unexpected client disconnect. Also found inconsistent handling of proxy 502/504 retries in the edge layer.

2026-03-04 16:22 - Design/UX: Provided guidance for UI to display 'partial output — trying to recover' state and not auto-submit to user until finalization marker received. Linked design note: https://confluence.redwood.ai/x/streaming-ui

2026-03-05 09:30 - Liam O'Connor: Proposed approach: (a) add 'stream_pos' and 'final' fields to SSE events, (b) hold generator state for a resume_window (30s) keyed by (client_key, request_id) and implement idempotent replay so replays start from stream_pos+1, (c) edge proxies return explicit 'Resume-Token' header on non-2xx disconnects to help client-side resume, (d) SDK helpers to backoff and use resume-token when available.

2026-03-06 13:12 - Security: Reviewed approach; no sensitive data persisted beyond resume_window; recommend encrypting resume tokens at rest. Security review completed with small KMS integration follow-up (ENG-9131).

2026-03-08 17:40 - Customer Success: Communicated interim mitigation to affected customers: enable client-side polling fallback, and temporary increase resume_window to 60s for their org ID. Collecting feedback.

Decided to implement adaptive resume-window (default 30s, lower under GC pressure) and add eviction hooks to free generator state earlier for small requests.

2026-03-10 18:05 - Liam O'Connor: Plan for rollout: feature-flag gate on runtime-1.20 -> enable gradually for Hosted customers with a 48-hour monitor; if metrics stable, flip globally. Add customer opt-in for extended resume_window.
2026-03-10 18:30 - Ops: Added alert 'sse.partial_deliveries > 0.1%' and dashboard pane for resume failure rate. Link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streams/sse-resume
resolution_plan: Implement server 'stream_pos' + resume token, hold generator state for a configurable resume_window (default 30s), add idempotent replay logic and eviction hooks; ship SDK helpers for safe resume/backoff; gate behind feature flag and rollout progressively; monitor metrics and rollback if memory/latency regressions exceed thresholds.
notes: Trade-offs: longer resume_window increases success for resume but raises memory pressure; adaptive window chosen to balance memory and customer experience.
Edge cases: clients that do not support resume will continue to see partial outputs; we'll recommend SDK upgrade and provide polling fallback in docs.
Follow-ups: ENG-9131 (KMS encrypt resume tokens), ENG-9130 (SDK integration tests), ENG-9212 (Private/Dedicated config parity planning)
